urn:eigenius:core:description: A scalar `value` claimed to lie within the closed interval [`lower`, `upper`]. The IntervalArithmetic institution's AutoOnLoad QueryClass dispatches a Julia handler (`validate_bounded_by`) that uses `IntervalArithmetic.jl` to verify the inclusion rigorously: `Holds` when the inclusion is proved, `Fails` when refuted, `Undecidable` when the proof is inconclusive. See D27 §4.0.2.
The scalar value being checked for interval membership.
Inclusive lower bound of the interval the value is claimed to lie within.
Inclusive upper bound of the interval the value is claimed to lie within.

A function over intervals — a `formulas:FormulaTerm` carried as the target shape of the IntervalArithmetic institution's `if_intv_function` ImportFormat. Symmetric on the IntervalArithmetic side to Symbolics' `SymbolicExpression`: both wrap a FormulaTerm. The `m = id` Comorphism between them realises D32 §6.2's identity-on-FormulaTerm bridge: the export and import payloads are bit-identical, so the typed middle is the identity Lambda.
The function's typed term — a `formulas:FormulaTerm` value (D32 §4). The chain validator type-checks the value against FormulaTerm's ctor schema at commit time.

Composite OnDemand input class for `qc_compute_bounds`: pairs a `SymbolicExpression` (whose `term` is a FormulaTerm) with a `BoundedBy` carrying the domain `[lower, upper]` for the free variable `x`. FIBER dispatch packs both arguments into a single typed resource because the institution-runtime boundary is unary; the institution destructures and runs interval-arithmetic over the domain.
The SymbolicExpression to interval-extend. Its `term` carries the FormulaTerm the institution walks under interval-arithmetic semantics.
Domain interval for the free variable `x`. Carried as a `BoundedBy` resource — its `lower` and `upper` define the evaluation range; `value` is unused on the input side of `qc_compute_bounds`.
